title: Theories of promissory liability
summary: The editors present several explanations for why some promises are enforced.
notes: Promise-centered accounts emphasize a promisor’s commitment; consent-based accounts emphasize an undertaking to incur legal obligation; reliance accounts emphasize induced change of position. Broader accounts discuss predictability and exchange, institutional enforcement, fairness, and the relationship between moral and legal obligation. The text places these perspectives together without announcing a single theory as the answer to every case. Distinguish an explanation of the institution from an element of an existing cause of action.
